text:
Darren Raddysh grew up in Toronto, went undrafted, and earned his way into the league with Tampa Bay, where last season he scored 22 goals and 70 points. Now he's a Maple Leaf, playing 24 minutes a night, and the first month has been mostly assists: 1 goal and 12 assists in 22 games, 8 of the points on the power play. The goal, his first as a Leaf, didn't come until November 10 against Colorado.

The shooting is the obvious soft spot. He's at 2% against a league norm of 6.2% for defensemen, but his own chance quality has also halved, from 0.52 expected goals per hour last season to 0.25. Some of last year's finishing was always going to fade without Tampa's teammates around him; Evolving-Hockey noted those teammates ranked in the 95th percentile.

The bigger picture is grim: Toronto has lost six straight, and at five on five the Leafs have had only 45.88% of the expected goals with Raddysh on. Watch whether he starts getting to the slot again; his 97.9 mph top shot says the tool is still there.
headline: Darren Raddysh's homecoming needs goals
